Communications with Jia on August 28 2023

"That's correct. My dataset is in the gi_JH4327 directory; it should contain JH4318 and JH4327.

JH4318 and JH4327 are not replicates. JH4318 contains four different datasets that were done on July 11, 2023. JH4327 contains another three unique datasets that were done on July 26, 2023. In total, there should be seven (4+3) datasets that were sequenced. I updated the metafile on Google drive detailing each dataset. Plese download all of them.

Out of these seven datasets, JH4327_01 is the most important one because it is the replicate for the 1538Cre TE10 HE13 dataset. The 1538Cre TE10 HE13 dataset that you have been analyzing has MGE, POA, and Septum mixed together (which you computationally filtered) and were done with the MULTIseq method. This JH4327_01 dataset contains only MGE cells and was done with just the 10x scRNAseq method (not MULTIseq).
"

Dataset info:
There are 3 datasets in this analysis: "1538TE10H11", "1538TE10H13", "JH4327_01_TE10H13", comparing 1538 cells treated with tamoxifen at E10, and harvested at E11 vs E13.The first two datasets are from a MULTIseq experiment.

Go to the line ~270 to load the integrated object:
pbmc <- readRDS("C:/Users/karol/Box/Nord_Lab_Computational_Projects3/Jia_E13_1538_Aug_2023/seurat_objects/MGE_1538_E11_and_E13_with_new_E13.Rds")


Three extra datasets from previous MULTIseq experiment:
 POA and Septum cells were removed from this object
 1538, E10, E11, MGE:
 Ex1_1538CreTE10HE11MGE <- readRDS(paste0("./Clustered Seurat objects/", "1538CreTE10HE11MGE", "_QCed_clustered_Seurat.RDS"))

 EX3_Pool22_MGE_1538CreTE10HE13 <- readRDS(paste0("./Clustered Seurat objects/", "1538CreTE10HE13_Pool22_MGE", "_QCed_clustered_Seurat.RDS"))

```{r}
# Load new datasets H13 dataset JH4327_01 containing 3525 cells (QCed by cell ranger) and perform basic QC


 # Load RNA counts
counts <- Read10X("C:/Users/karol/Box/Nord_Lab_Computational_Projects3/Jia_E13_1538_Aug_2023/JH4327_01/outs/filtered_feature_bc_matrix")

sample = "JH4327_01"

    # Create a Seurat object containing the RNA data
    pbmc <- CreateSeuratObject(
        counts = counts,
        assay = "RNA"
    )

    # Check names of the mitochondrial genes
    # rownames(pbmc)[grepl("^mt-", rownames(pbmc), ignore.case = TRUE)]

    # Mitochondrial genes:
    DefaultAssay(pbmc) <- "RNA"
    pbmc[["percent.mt"]] <- PercentageFeatureSet(pbmc, pattern = "^mt-")

    # Violin plot - pre-filtering
    p1 <- VlnPlot(
        object = pbmc,
        features = c("nCount_RNA", "nFeature_RNA", "percent.mt"),
        ncol = 3,
        pt.size = 0.1)&
        theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())&
        plot_annotation(title = paste0(sample, ", Cellranger filtered cells.", " Features: ", nrow(pbmc),
                                       " Cells: ", ncol(pbmc)),
                        theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold")))


    p3 <- ggplot(pbmc@meta.data, aes(x = log2(nFeature_RNA),  y = log(nCount_RNA)))+
        geom_point(alpha = 0.1)+
        theme_bw()+
        labs(title = "Cellranger filtered cells")




    # Define QC filtering thresholds using 3 median absolute deviations.
    # This idea borrowed from the scater package

    #count_threshold_high <- median(pbmc@meta.data$nCount_RNA) + mad_distance*mad(pbmc@meta.data$nCount_RNA)
    #features_threshold_high <- median(pbmc@meta.data$nFeature_RNA) + mad_distance*mad(pbmc@meta.data$nFeature_RNA)
    #mito_threshold_high <- median(pbmc@meta.data$percent.mt) + mad_distance*mad(pbmc@meta.data$percent.mt)

    # This approach to filtering is not used here. To keep consistent criteria across multiple datasets
    # we decided to keep cells with > 1000 reads and < 20% mito reads
    mad_distance = 5

    pbmc[["nCount_RNA_abv_1000"]] <- pbmc@meta.data$nCount_RNA > 1000
    pbmc[["nCount_RNA_less_than_5_MADs"]] <- pbmc@meta.data$nCount_RNA <
                                             median(pbmc@meta.data$nCount_RNA) + mad_distance*mad(pbmc@meta.data$nCount_RNA)

    pbmc[["nCount_RNA_abv_1000_and_less_than_5_MADs"]] <- pbmc[["nCount_RNA_abv_1000"]] &
                                                          pbmc[["nCount_RNA_less_than_5_MADs"]]


    pbmc[["nFeature_RNA_abv_200"]] <- pbmc@meta.data$nFeature_RNA > 200
    pbmc[["nFeature_RNA_less_than_5_MADs"]] <- pbmc@meta.data$nFeature_RNA <
                                               median(pbmc@meta.data$nFeature_RNA) + mad_distance*mad(pbmc@meta.data$nFeature_RNA)

    pbmc[["nFeature_RNA_abv_200_and_less_than_5_MADs"]] <- pbmc[["nFeature_RNA_abv_200"]] &
                                                           pbmc[["nFeature_RNA_less_than_5_MADs"]]

    pbmc[["percent.mt_less_than_15"]] <- pbmc@meta.data$percent.mt < 15


    ######
    pbmc[["Cell_passing_QC"]] <- pbmc[["nCount_RNA_abv_1000_and_less_than_5_MADs"]] &
                                 pbmc[["nFeature_RNA_abv_200_and_less_than_5_MADs"]] &
                                 pbmc[["percent.mt_less_than_15"]]


    # Perform manual QC
    ## Filter out low quality cells
    pbmc <- subset(
        x = pbmc,
        subset =
            #nCount_RNA < count_threshold_high &
            nCount_RNA > 1000 &
            #nFeature_RNA < features_threshold_high &
            #nFeature_RNA > 200 &
            percent.mt < 20
    )


    # Violin plot - post-filtering
    p2 <- VlnPlot(
        object = pbmc,
        features = c("nCount_RNA", "nFeature_RNA", "percent.mt"),
        ncol = 3,
        pt.size = 0.1)&
        theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())&
        plot_annotation(title = paste0(sample, ", Quality filtered cells.", " Features: ", nrow(pbmc),
                                       " Cells: ", ncol(pbmc)),
                        theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold")))


    p4 <- ggplot(pbmc@meta.data, aes(x = log2(nFeature_RNA),  y = log(nCount_RNA)))+
        geom_point(alpha = 0.1)+
        theme_bw()+
        labs(title = "Quality filtered cells")



    # Save post filtering object
# saveRDS(pbmc, file = paste0("C:/Users/karol/Box/Nord_Lab_Computational_Projects3/Jia_E13_1538_Aug_2023/seurat_objects/", sample, "_QCed_Seurat_obj.rds"))


   top <-  plot_grid(p1, p2, ncol = 1)

   bottom <- plot_grid(p3, p4, ncol = 2)

   plot_grid(top, bottom, ncol = 1)
```

Integrate and cluster data
```{r}

# Rerun the integration pipeline to insure that all object slots are updated


# Add dataset IDs
pbmc_old$age <- ifelse(pbmc_old$dataset == "1538TE10H11", "E11", "E13")

pbmc$dataset <- "JH4327_01_TE10H13"
pbmc$age <- "E13"


# Initial clustering in the new data

pbmc <- SCTransform(pbmc, method = "glmGamPoi", verbose = FALSE)
pbmc <- RunPCA(pbmc, features = VariableFeatures(object = pbmc))


pbmc <- RunUMAP(pbmc, dims = 1:25, verbose = FALSE)
pbmc <- FindNeighbors(pbmc, dims = 1:25, verbose = FALSE)
pbmc <- FindClusters(pbmc, verbose = FALSE)

DimPlot(pbmc)

```




```{r}

# Create a list of objects and integrate
ifnb.list <- list(pbmc_old, pbmc)
ifnb.list <- lapply(X = ifnb.list, FUN = SCTransform)

features <- SelectIntegrationFeatures(object.list = ifnb.list, nfeatures = 3000)
ifnb.list <- PrepSCTIntegration(object.list = ifnb.list, anchor.features = features)


gc()

# Check the number of cells. If few cells are present adjust the k.weight parameter accordingly.
sapply(ifnb.list, function(x) ncol(x)) # 4438 + 3347 cells


plan("multicore", workers = 1) # Decrease the number of cores if running out of memory or "Error 2 (The system cannot find the file specified)" ?? I'm not sure what this error means, but it's triggered by FindIntegrationAnchors.
options(future.globals.maxSize = 30000 * 1024^2) # for 30 Gb RAM

RNA.anchors <- FindIntegrationAnchors(object.list = ifnb.list,
                                         normalization.method = "SCT",
                                         anchor.features = features)

# k.weight adjustment: https://github.com/satijalab/seurat/issues/3930
RNA_integrated <- IntegrateData(anchorset = RNA.anchors,
                                normalization.method = "SCT",
                                k.weight = 100)  # 100 is the default value

RNA_integrated <- RunPCA(RNA_integrated, verbose = TRUE, npcs = 30)

source("data_dims_simple.R")
data_dims_scree(RNA_integrated)


PCs = 25 # Determined empirically

pbmc <- RNA_integrated
rm(RNA_integrated)
rm(pbmc_old)

pbmc <- RunPCA(pbmc, verbose = FALSE, npcs = PCs)
pbmc <- RunUMAP(pbmc, dims = 1:PCs, verbose = FALSE)

# Recluster
pbmc <- FindNeighbors(pbmc, dims = 1:PCs, verbose = FALSE)
pbmc <- FindClusters(pbmc, verbose = FALSE, graph.name = "integrated_snn")

DimPlot(pbmc)

DimPlot(pbmc, split.by = "dataset", label = TRUE, label.size = 8, pt.size = 1.1)
```

```{r}
volcano_plot_text <- function(x, title) {


ggplot(x, aes(x = avg_log2FC, y=-log10(p_val), color = DE_Dir, label = gene_name)) +
        geom_point(size=1, alpha=0.5, stroke = 0.5)+
        theme_light()+
        #geom_vline(xintercept = 1.5, linetype = 2)+
        #geom_vline(xintercept = -1.5, linetype = 2)+
        geom_text_repel(data = VZ_markers[1:50,], show.legend = FALSE)+

        labs(title= title, y="-log10(P)", x="logFC")+
        theme(plot.title = element_text(size = rel(2), hjust=0.5))+
        theme(axis.text=element_text(size=14))+
        theme(legend.title=element_blank())+
        theme(axis.text=element_text(size=14))+
        theme(axis.title = element_text(size=14, face = "bold"))+
       theme(legend.position = c(0.87, 0.08),
          legend.background = element_rect(color = "black", size = 0, linetype = "solid"),
          legend.key.size = unit(0.5, "lines"),
          legend.key.height = unit(1.2, "lines"),
          legend.key.width = unit(1.2, "lines"),
          legend.margin = margin(1, 3, 1, 2)) +
    guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3)))

}
```

GSEA

```{r}

library(clusterProfiler)
library(org.Mm.eg.db)
library(enrichplot)
library(BiocParallel)


gsea_plot <- function(data, title){

  df <- data

  # Rank usign a combination of P values and logFC
  # rank from lowest to highest values
  #df$Rank <- -log10(df$PValue) * df$logFC

  df$Rank <- -log10(df$avg_log2FC)

  # Create a named vector of log2 fold changes
  gene_list <- df$Rank
  names(gene_list) <- df$gene_name
  gene_list <- sort(gene_list, decreasing = TRUE)


  param <- MulticoreParam(workers = 12)

  gsea_result <- gseGO(
    geneList = gene_list,
    OrgDb = org.Mm.eg.db,
    keyType = "SYMBOL",
    ont = "BP",    # Set the parameter to All
    minGSSize = 10,
    maxGSSize = 2000,
    pvalueCutoff = 1,
    verbose = TRUE,
    seed = 123,
    BPPARAM = param)


  #gsea_result
  p1 <- dotplot(gsea_result, showCategory = 30) +
    aes(fill = ifelse(NES > 0, "positive", "negative")) +
    geom_point(aes(color = ifelse(NES > 0, "positive", "negative")), size = 3, stroke = 1.5) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("positive" = "red", "negative" = "blue")) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("positive" = "red", "negative" = "blue")) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(fill = "NES Direction", color = "NES Direction") +
    ggtitle(title)+
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = rel(2)))


  list(gsea_result, p1)

}
```

```{r}

#marker_DE, dev_class_int

marker_heatmap <- function(marker_DE, dev_class_int, title){

# Cluster genes
d <- subset(pbmc, dataset %in% c("1538TE10H11", "1538TE10H13", "JH4327_01_TE10H13"))@assays$SCT@counts

wl_genes <- marker_DE$gene_name[!grepl("mt-|Rps|Rpl", marker_DE$gene_name)]

top_positive <- filter(marker_DE, gene_name %in% wl_genes, avg_log2FC > 0)$gene_name[1:50]
top_negative <- filter(marker_DE, gene_name %in% wl_genes, avg_log2FC < 0)$gene_name[1:50]

d <- d[rownames(d) %in% c(top_positive, top_negative), ]
d <- as.matrix(d)


paletteLength <- 100
test <- as.matrix(d)

myBreaks <- c(seq(min(test), 0, length.out=ceiling(paletteLength/2) + 1),
              seq(max(test)/paletteLength, max(test), length.out=floor(paletteLength/2)))

myColor <- colorRampPalette(c("#9E0041", "#fea11d","#fea11d",
                              "white",
                              "#43abea", "#0a48aa", "#13008e"))(paletteLength)

# Cluster annotation
anno <- subset(pbmc, dataset %in% c("1538TE10H11", "1538TE10H13", "JH4327_01_TE10H13"))@meta.data
anno <- as.data.frame(anno[,c("dataset", "Dev_classes", "seurat_clusters", "age")])


anno$seurat_clusters <- factor(anno$seurat_clusters, levels = 0:max(as.numeric(pbmc@meta.data$seurat_clusters)))


d2 <- lapply(c("VZ", "SVZ", "MZ"), function(y){

        lapply(c("1538TE10H11", "1538TE10H13", "JH4327_01_TE10H13"), function(x){

    cells <- rownames(filter(anno, Dev_classes == y, dataset == x))
    as.data.frame(d)[, cells]

    })
    })


d21 <- do.call(cbind, c(d2[[dev_class_int]]))

# Work Zone
library(pheatmap)

d3 <- t(scale(t(d21)))
d3 <- ifelse(d3 > 3, 3, d3)
d3 <- ifelse(d3 < -3, -3, d3)

# VZ
VZ_pheatmap <- pheatmap(d3,
         fontsize = 8,
         show_rownames = T,
         show_colnames = F,
         labels_col = F,
         cluster_cols = F,
         clustering_distance_rows = "correlation",
         clustering_distance_cols = "correlation",
         method = "average",
         color = rev(myColor),
         annotation_col = anno,
         main = title)

}

```

```{r}

# Assuming 'pbmc' is your Seurat object and 'genes' is your data frame of gene markers
ptime_axis <- c(2, 15, 7, 14, 5, 12, 9, 11, 1, 3, 0, 16, 4, 8, 6, 13, 10)

# Combine all genes into a single vector
gene_vector <- unique(as.vector(as.matrix(genes)))

# Filter gene_vector to include only genes present in the pbmc object
gene_vector <- gene_vector[gene_vector %in% rownames(pbmc@assays$SCT@data)]

# Extract the expression matrix from the Seurat object
expression_matrix <- as.matrix(pbmc@assays$SCT@data[gene_vector, ])

# Create a list to store reordered columns
reordered_columns <- list()

# Loop through each cluster in ptime_axis and cbind the cells
for (cluster in ptime_axis) {
    cluster_cells <- colnames(pbmc)[pbmc$seurat_clusters == cluster]
    if (length(cluster_cells) > 0) {
        reordered_columns[[as.character(cluster)]] <- expression_matrix[, cluster_cells, drop = FALSE]
    }
}

# Combine all columns into a single matrix
reordered_matrix <- do.call(cbind, reordered_columns)

# Create the heatmap using ComplexHeatmap
if (!requireNamespace("ComplexHeatmap", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("ComplexHeatmap")
}
library(ComplexHeatmap)

Heatmap(reordered_matrix,
        name = "Expression",
        show_row_names = TRUE,
        show_column_names = TRUE,
        cluster_rows = TRUE,
        cluster_columns = FALSE,
        column_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 10),
        row_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 10))

```

```{r}
#Do DE analysis between the two ages (E11.5 vs E13.5) for each individual VZ clusters: 2, 7, 5, and 14.



DE_tables <- lapply(c(2, 7, 5, 14, 9, 11, 1, 3, 8), function(x){

    DefaultAssay(pbmc) <- "SCT"
    pbmc <- PrepSCTFindMarkers(pbmc)

    df <- FindMarkers(pbmc, ident.1 = rownames(filter(pbmc@meta.data,
                                              seurat_clusters == x, age == "E11")),
                                ident.2 = rownames(filter(pbmc@meta.data,
                                              seurat_clusters == x, age == "E13")),
                                min.pct = 0.25,
                                logfc.threshold = 0.25,
                                only.pos = FALSE)


    df$gene_name <- rownames(df)

    df$DE_Dir <- ifelse(df$avg_log2FC > 0, "Up_at_E11", "Up_at_E13")

    write.csv(df, paste0("./Jia_1st_paper_supp_tables/E11_vs_E13_cluster_", x, ".csv"), row.names = F)

    df
    })


names(DE_tables) <- c(2, 7, 5, 14, 9, 11, 1, 3, 8)

names(DE_tables)


#### Sanity check for directionality of color annotation
#VlnPlot(subset(pbmc, seurat_clusters == 11),
#        features = rownames(filter(DE_tables[[6]], avg_log2FC > 0))[1:20], group.by = "age")



library(ggrepel)


volcano_plot_text <- function(x, title) {


ggplot(x, aes(x = avg_log2FC, y=-log10(p_val), color = DE_Dir, label = gene_name)) +
        geom_point(size=1, alpha=0.5, stroke = 0.5)+
        theme_light()+
        #geom_vline(xintercept = 1.5, linetype = 2)+
        #geom_vline(xintercept = -1.5, linetype = 2)+
        geom_text_repel(data = x[1:200,], show.legend = FALSE)+

        labs(title= title, y="-log10(P)", x="logFC")+
        theme(plot.title = element_text(size = rel(2), hjust=0.5))+
        theme(axis.text=element_text(size=14))+
        theme(legend.title=element_blank())+
        theme(axis.text=element_text(size=14))+
        theme(axis.title = element_text(size=14, face = "bold"))+
       theme(legend.position = c(0.87, 0.08),
          legend.background = element_rect(color = "black", size = 0, linetype = "solid"),
          legend.key.size = unit(0.5, "lines"),
          legend.key.height = unit(1.2, "lines"),
          legend.key.width = unit(1.2, "lines"),
          legend.margin = margin(1, 3, 1, 2)) +
    guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3)))

}
```

* Transcription factors such as Gsx2 and Nkx2-1 mark VZ progenitor cells of the LGE/CGE/septum and MGE/POA, respectively (Guillemot, 2005, Sussel et al., 1999, Toresson et al., 2000a, Toresson et al., 2000b, Waclaw et al., 2009, Yun et al., 2003).

* As cells mature within the VZ, they express transcription factors such as Ascl1 (Mash1), and then Dlx2 (Yun et al., 2002). Dlx2+ cells form “radial” columns within the VZ that connect with the underlying SVZ that has homogeneous Dlx2 expression (see below; Eisenstat et al., 1999, Porteus et al., 1994).


* The VZ primary progenitors generate a secondary progenitor zone, the SVZ, which is particularly large in the basal ganglia anlage. There are at least two parts of the SVZ (SVZ1 and SVZ2) based on the density of mitotically active cells and the expression of Ascl1, Dlx2, Gsx2, and Olig2 transcription factors, and markers of neuronal maturation (Eisenstat et al., 1999, Petryniak et al., 2007, Yun et al., 2002). It is likely that SVZ1 and SVZ2 represent progressive states in maturation. The SVZ1 consists of a thin layer of proliferative cells immediately below the VZ; it shows strong expression of Dlx2 and often expresses genes that are markers of the VZ (e.g., Ascl1, Gsx2, and Olig2) (Petryniak et al., 2007, Wang et al., 2011, Yun et al., 2002). The SVZ2 forms later than SVZ1 (Yun et al., 2002) and is a larger and more differentiated zone consisting of a mixture of mitotically active and postmitotic cells; this region continues to express Dlx2 but shows much lower expression of Gsx2 and Ascl1. Currently, it is unknown whether SVZ1 and SVZ2 progenitors have distinct cell biology.

* The mantle zone (MZ) is the most superficial layer and consists primarily of neurons at various stages of migration and differentiation (it also contains oligodendrocytes, blood vessels, and later astrocytes)

* For instance, the LGE generates olfactory bulb interneurons, the MGE and POA generate striatal interneurons, and the MGE, POA, and dCGE generate cortical interneurons.

* The vast majority of neurons generated in the basal ganglia are GABAergic. Thus, the transcriptional code for generating these neurons has at its core the ability to express the enzymes that defines GABAergic neurons, such as GAD1, GAD2, and vGAT. As will be described more below, the Ascl1, Gsx2, and Dlx1,2,5,6 transcription factors have fundamental roles in specifying GABAergic properties of basal ganglia neurons. Dlx genes are implicated in directly regulating GAD1, GAD2, and vGAT (Le et al., 2017, Long et al., 2007, Long et al., 2009a, Pla et al., 2017). The basal ganglia also generate cholinergic neurons under the control of Islet1, Lhx8, and Nkx2-1, and dopaminergic neurons under the control of Dlx1&2 and Pax6.


* The GEs also generate oligodendrocytes and astrocytes that contribute to the cellular organization of the basal ganglia (and overlying cerebral cortex). Oligodendrogenesis requires the function of the Olig transcription factors and is repressed by the Dlx transcription factors. Conversely, Olig1&2 repress Dlx expression (Silbereis et al., 2014). Ascl1 interacts with these fate decisions by repressing Dlx expression noncell autonomously through Notch signaling (Petryniak et al., 2007). Gsx1&2 factors also serve as negative regulators of oligodendrocyte specification within VZ progenitors, thus promoting a neuronal fate in their subsequent progeny (Chapman et al., 2013, Chapman et al., 2018).
